# Draft:Joel Edwards (British singer)

Joel Edwards
Joel Edwards is a British singer, songwriter, producer, and remixer, best known as the vocalist and co-writer of the electronic music act Deepest Blue, whose 2003 debut single "Deepest Blue" reached the UK Top 10. He has also released music under various aliases and collaborated with a wide range of artists across electronic, pop, and dance genres.
Early Career
Edwards began his career in the early 2000s working with UK garage producer Ed Case, co-writing on the album ''Ed's Guest List (2002). The album featured contributions from artists including Ming Xia (Spooks), Saffron (Republica), and Shaun Escoffery, who later starred as Mufasa in The Lion King (musical) in London’s West End.
Deepest Blue
In 2003, Edwards co-founded Deepest Blue with producer Matt Schwartz. Their debut single "Deepest Blue" peaked at No. 7 on the UK Singles Chart. Follow-up singles "Give It Away" and "Is It a Sin?" reached No. 9 and No. 24, respectively. The track "Shooting Star" was later used as the theme music for Sky Sports football coverage and charted at No. 57.
Their debut album, Late September (2004), reached No. 22 on the UK Albums Chart. The album artwork was created by Storm Thorgerson, the legendary designer known for his work with Pink Floyd, and parts of the album were recorded aboard David Gilmour’s studio boat, The Astoria.
Solo Career
In 2008, Edwards signed a solo recording deal with Mercury Records and recorded an album titled Lost and Found''. The project featured a full orchestra conducted by Simon Hale, and included contributions from Georgie Fame, Ralph Salmins (drums), Steve Pearce (bass), and Simon Carter (keyboards). The album was never released due to internal label restructuring and the departure of Edwards’ A&R and Managing Director.
Other Musical Projects
Edwards has released music under various aliases, including TrAmHeD, London Fields, DEE-LUX, and Dead Guys. From 2009–2010, he served as the live frontman for Planet Funk, standing in for Dan Black during European shows.
He also co-wrote and produced the track "This Time" for Melanie C, best known as "Sporty Spice" of the Spice Girls.
Remix and Production Work
As a remixer and producer, Edwards has worked with or remixed:
* Pixie Lott – "Turn It Up"
* Blondie – "Good Boys"
* Lamb – "Wonder"
* Chicane – "Locking Down"
* Texas – "Can't Resist"
* Sway – "Party Like Ur 18"
His work has been remixed by:
* Eric Prydz
* Ferry Corsten
* Goom Gum
* Fred V
* DJEFF
* Jon Hopkins
In 2021, Russian duo Filatov & Karas released "Give It Away x Deepest Blue", which was certified Platinum in Poland.
Advertising Work
In addition to his recording career, Edwards has composed and produced music for international advertising campaigns, including work for Samsung, Ford, and Littlewoods.
Labels and Affiliations
Edwards has released music through:
* Ministry of Sound
* Armada Music
* Mercury Records
* Universal Music Group
* Sony Music
* Warner Music Group
* [https://www.zrecords.ltd Z Records] (founded by Dave Lee)
* Toolroom Records
